subject.declared_domain: The C2/C3-in-graph MATERIALIZE SPEC writer: emits proposed node + CONTAINS-edge records (C2Motif class nodes, C3System nodes, C3->C2 and C2->C1 CONTAINS edges) as ONE json artifact for 0.7.0_AE_CloudOps to ingest into the estate graph. It is a SPEC EMITTER, not an ingester: it writes no graph, opens no store, and performs no promotion. Its declared domain stops at the file it writes.

methodology.how: A single build_spec() pass over two upstream catalogs plus a decompression ladder. It iterates NFRA_MOTIF_P1_c2_catalog.CATALOG, calls P1.build_motif(spec) per entry and RETAINS ONLY those whose recurrence >= P1.AC3_THRESHOLD; the surviving motifs become C2Motif node records. For each it derives the C1 layer via comp_ladder.decompress(motif) filtered to layer=='C1', canonicalises each C1 nid by stripping the ladder discriminator, DEDUPES by canonical target while merging the detector provenance into props.via_detectors, and emits one C2->C1 CONTAINS edge per distinct target. It then loads the cluster index and shares-source from NFRA_MOTIF_P2_c3_emergence, builds C3 systems over the retained motif nodes, and emits a C3System node plus one C3->C2 CONTAINS edge per member. The return is a single dict carrying producer/consumer/cert/grounding strings, a convention_note, a taxonomy_prereq block, a counts block and the nodes and edges arrays; main() serialises it with json.dump(indent=2).

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: On P1.GraphUnavailable: main() catches it at :154, prints 'SPEC NOT REGENERATED -- graph unavailable: <ex>' plus a fail-closed note to stderr/stdout, RETURNS EXIT CODE 2, and does NOT open the artifact for write. The previous motif_c2c3_materialize.json is left exactly as it was. No other exception is caught: any other failure propagates as an uncaught traceback before the write, so a partial file is not produced either.
silent_degrade_paths: THE PRIMARY ONE: a failed run and a run that never happened leave BYTE-IDENTICAL state on disk. The fail-closed branch's whole purpose is to preserve the last-good artifact, so after it fires the artifact is unchanged -- which is also what you get by not running the script at all. Only the exit code and the stdout line distinguish them, and both are ephemeral: nothing durable records that a regeneration was attempted and refused.

The emitted artifact carries no emitted_at, no run id and no input vintage: its `grounding` block pins upstream COMMITS (c2_catalog_cert, c3_emergence, graph fix-verified) but not the moment or the graph state of the run. A reader of the file alone cannot date it except by filesystem or git metadata external to it.
Because the script has no cadence and no trigger, the fail-closed guard is CORRECT AND UNREACHABLE in the live estate: it protects a regeneration path that nothing invokes.
failure_mode.evidence: Read at source :146-170 @c0dc3f09a0; the except clause is :154, the refusal prints :157-158, `return 2` at :159, and the write at :160-161 is reachable ONLY on the non-exception path. The 'no' verdict on distinguishability is a structural read of that control flow, not a run: there is no field in the artifact and no sidecar that records an attempted-and-refused regeneration, so the artifact plane cannot separate the two states. NOT EXERCISED: I did not induce a GraphUnavailable to watch it fire -- doing so would require making the graph unreachable, which is out of this TO's no-deploy/no-infra scope. The branch is therefore READ, not RUN, and that limit is stated rather than papered over.

verdict.why: The script is internally sound and does the careful things well: it fails closed rather than writing a partial spec, it canonicalises across two identity spaces with the conversion verified at the store, and it preserves detector provenance through a dedupe that would otherwise lose it. What qualifies it is not a defect in the code but the gap between what it is and how the estate uses it. THREE QUALIFYING FACTS, each measured above: (1) the script has NO cadence and NO trigger -- nothing invokes it -- while the artifact it wrote in July is read on every derive, so a frozen output is load-bearing and its writer is dormant; (2) its failure mode is not distinguishable from a genuine negative on the artifact plane, and its fail-closed guard is unreachable in the live estate precisely because nothing calls it; (3) the artifact carries no self-dating field, so its age is knowable only from metadata outside it. None of these makes the current output wrong. Together they mean nothing in the system would notice if it became wrong.
blocking_defects: NOT A DEFECT IN THIS SUBJECT, RAISED AGAINST ANOTHER ARTIFACT AND ROUTED: the D11 graph_object_manifest.json entry for part 'motif_c2c3_materialize.json' carries basis 'measured' and the evidence line 'Emits 19 C2Motif CLASS nodes.' The artifact it cards emits 6. Verified on the identical file -- same home path, same 15,255 bytes, same commit fad55a83c7, all three matching the manifest's own identifiers -- and counted three independent ways (self-reported counts field, recount of the nodes array, distinct node_id set), all 6. The A/B sibling emits 13. 6 + 13 = 19, so the manifest row appears to attribute the SUM OF BOTH SPEC ARTIFACTS to one of them. A total that ties can hide a wrong split. This is surfaced to 3.0.0_SA_CVO~X cc the issuer per this TO's off-spec clause; it is NOT remediated here, and it does not block this card.
